final.summary: Recommended: fused. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.93 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.06 °C, 91% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **This plan gets most of the important work done (about 91%) but runs close to the heat limit.** At its hottest, a worker's body temperature is expected to come within a tenth of a degree of the safe limit, so there's almost no room for surprises. Watch the crew closely, enforce breaks, and pull people back if the day runs hotter than forecast.

**Rosa is new and her body isn't used to working in this heat yet.** She shouldn't do the heaviest jobs during the hot part of the day. Others will need to cover those tasks while she builds up her tolerance.

**There are two other options, each with a trade-off.** A safer plan keeps everyone cooler (peak about 37.8 °C) but finishes less work (86%). Moving the cable pulling to the cool morning gets slightly more done (92%) but runs even closer to the heat limit (about 37.97 °C). The current plan sits between the two.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
